{{Short description|Canadian statistician (1837–1911)}}
{{Other people||George Johnson (disambiguation){{!}}George Johnson}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=September 2025}}
'''George Johnson''' (1837–1911) was a Canadian statistician. He was born in [[Annapolis Royal, Nova Scotia]] in 1837. For some years he was the Editor of ''The Halifax Reporter'' and was subsequently the Ottawa correspondent for ''[[The Toronto Mail]]''. From 1891 to 1904 he was the Dominion Statistician. He also edited the Canada Year Book from 1886 to 1904. He was the author of a number of works, including ''The Handbook of Canada'' and ''Alphabet of First Things in Canada''. He was an honorary Fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] and died in 1911.<ref>{{Cite web |last=<!--Not stated--> |title=George Johnson fonds |date=25 November 2016 |url=https://recherche-collection-search.bac-lac.gc.ca/eng/home/record?app=fonandcol&IdNumber=105597}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Library and Archives Canada / Bibliothèque et Archives Canada |url=https://heritage.canadiana.ca/view/oocihm.lac_mikan_105597}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Worton |first=David A. |url=https://www.mqup.ca/dominion-bureau-of-statistics--the-products-9780773516601.php |title=Dominion Bureau of Statistics : A History of Canada's Central Statistical Office and Its Antecedents, 1841-1972 |publisher=The Institute of Public Administration in Canada / [[McGill-Queen's University Press]] |publication-place=Montreal and Kingston |publication-date=1998 |pages=409}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Prévost |first=Jean-Guy |author-link=Jean-Guy Prévost |date=9 June 2020 |title=Past, present and future of Canadian statistics |url=https://content.iospress.com/articles/statistical-journal-of-the-iaos/sji190601 |journal=Statistical Journal of the IAOS |language=English |volume=36 |issue=2 |pages=355–363 |doi=10.3233/SJI-190601 |issn=1875-9254 |access-date=1 August 2024}}</ref>
